newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says lira bond issue builds yield curve.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says lira bond issue builds yield curve.

text.p: Mexico said on Wednesday that its issue this week of a seven-year lira bond would help future Mexican issuers by building a yield curve similar to the one it has established in dollars.
On Tuesday, Mexico launched a 500 million seven-year lira bond with a coupon of 8.375 percent via Chase Securities and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

"The federal government has taken advantage of prevailing market conditions to create a lira yield curve similar to that which exists in the dollar market, thereby creating a benchmark for other Mexican issuers," the finance ministry said.
"Over the last few months, the Italian market has become one of the major sources of liquidity at a global level for borrowers like Mexico," it added.
This week's issue follows three previous 500 million lira bonds issued at a 20-year maturity in April, 10 years in January and five years in November 1996.

The proceeds of Tuesday's bond issue will be put towards the expected amortization of $6 billion in bank notes on August 6, the ministry said in a statement. ((-- Caroline Brothers, Mexico City newsroom +525 728 7905))
